刘易斯·汉密尔顿和夏尔·勒克莱尔将于本周末在蒙扎使用全新的升级引擎；汉密尔顿希望主队能“为胜利而战”；请通过天空体育F1频道观看意大利大奖赛的全部比赛环节，从周五上午11点30分和下午3点的练习赛开始
当法拉利车迷齐聚米兰为F1车手加油时，刘易斯·汉密尔顿和夏尔·勒克莱尔受到了热烈欢迎，活动是在Peroni Nastro Azzurro 0.0%之家举办的一场活动
刘易斯·汉密尔顿希望法拉利能拥有在主场意大利大奖赛上争夺胜利的赛车，这个周末他们将为两位车手引入发动机升级。
这次升级将是法拉利本赛季在动力单元方面的第二次升级，此前国际汽联（FIA）批准了他们两次研发机会。
法拉利去年在蒙扎经历了令人失望的一站，分别获得第四名和第六名，但在2026年这个竞争更激烈的赛季中，他们仍有机会争夺世界冠军，因此今年的期望更高。

汉密尔顿与迈克尔·舒马赫共同保持着五次意大利大奖赛夺冠的纪录，但去年他作为法拉利车手在蒙扎的首秀上仅获得第六名，当时他正处于身穿红色战袍的首个艰难赛季之中。
这位英国车手在六月的西班牙大奖赛上为法拉利赢得了首场胜利，现在他将在法拉利的主场赛道上寻求第二场胜利；这个周末，梅赛德斯的积分榜领先者安东内利因引擎受罚将从发车区的最后一位起步。
法拉利的刘易斯·汉密尔顿在巴塞罗那-加泰罗尼亚大奖赛上夺得了他身穿红色战袍以来的首场胜利
"巴塞罗那太棒了，感谢所有人的支持，"汉密尔顿补充道，他目前落后安东内利59分。
"但我希望这个周末我们能争夺一场胜利。"
汉密尔顿和队友夏尔·勒克莱尔在皇家宫（Palazzo Reale）活动现场受到了车迷们的热烈欢呼，这位英国车手说："能来到这里真是太棒了。这是第二年，看到你们都在这里真是难以置信。
"看到你们都在这里让我非常感动。我爱车迷（Tifosi）。"
法拉利发布了其一次性涂装，向迈克尔·舒马赫致敬，用于在蒙扎举行的F1意大利大奖赛
引擎升级将在多大程度上提升法拉利的胜算？
这次升级将是法拉利本赛季在动力单元方面的第二次升级，此前国际汽联（FIA）批准了他们两次研发机会。
一级方程式2026年的新动力单元规则允许发动机厂商在内燃机性能落后的情况下进行升级。
在今年早些时候进行的首次额外研发与升级机会（ADUO）审查之后，法拉利被认为落后于标杆发动机厂商红牛超过百分之四。
法拉利在六月的奥地利大奖赛上引入了他们的第一次发动机升级，并将在蒙扎的主场赛事中为两辆赛车带来第二次升级。
在《F1秀》播客节目中，哈里·本杰明认为，尽管结果令人沮丧，刘易斯·汉密尔顿仍能从荷兰大奖赛中收获积极的因素。
这意味着汉密尔顿和勒克莱尔将启用本赛季的第四台发动机，这也是在遭受任何发车位处罚之前的最后一台。
“在性能方面，我们将推出一套升级版动力单元，这是 允许的发动机研发配额框架下可用的发展机会的一部分，”法拉利车队领队弗雷德里克·瓦塞尔说。
“这代表着朝着正确方向迈出的一步，而且我们都知道，今年的一切都在于微小的收益提升。蒙扎是一条对赛车要求极高的赛道，各车队的差距极其接近，我们的首要任务是从周五开始，把整个周末的每一个环节都做到最好。”
“我们希望从主场车迷的热情中汲取额外的动力，为我们的蒂福西（tifosi，指车队忠实粉丝）奉献一个强大的周末。”

detailEn: Italian GP: Lewis Hamilton hopeful Ferrari can fight for Monza win as team confirm engine upgrade for home race

Lewis Hamilton and Charles Leclerc will run a new, upgraded engine at Monza this weekend; Hamilton hopeful home team "can fight for a win"; watch every session of the Italian GP live on Sky Sports F1, starting with Friday's practice sessions at 11.30am and 3pm
Lewis Hamilton and Charles Leclerc were greeted with a big reception as Ferrari fans gathered in Milan to cheer on the F1 stars at a House of Peroni Nastro Azzurro 0.0% event
Lewis Hamilton hopes Ferrari have the car to fight for the win at their home Italian Grand Prix, a weekend in which they will introduce an engine upgrade for both drivers.
The upgrade will be Ferrari's second on the power unit side this season after they were granted two development opportunities by the FIA.
Ferrari endured a disappointing Monza last year, finishing fourth and sixth, but hopes are higher for 2026 amid a more competitive season in which they remain in world title contention.

Speaking at a House of Peroni Nastro Azzurro 0.0% event in central Milan in front of the Tifosi on Wednesday evening, Hamilton said: "It's always exciting in Monza. It's the fastest race we get to go to.
"Last year we didn't have the car to fight. I think this year we have the car to fight."

Hamilton shares the record of five Italian Grand Prix wins with Michael Schumacher but he finished only sixth on his Monza debut as a Ferrari driver last year amid a difficult first campaign in red.

The Briton won his first race for them at June's Spanish Grand Prix and now goes in search of a second at Ferrari's home track on a weekend that Mercedes' championship leader Kimi Antonelli will start at the back of the grid due to an engine penalty.
Ferrari's Lewis Hamilton claimed his first win in red at the Barcelona-Catalunya Grand Prix
"Barcelona was amazing, the support from everybody," added Hamilton, who trails Antonelli by 59 points.
"But I hope this weekend we can fight for a win."

Hamilton and team-mate Charles Leclerc received a huge ovation from the fans attending the event in the Palazzo Reale, with the Briton saying: "It's amazing to be here. This is the second year and to see you all here is incredible.
"To see you all here is overwhelming. I love the Tifosi."
Ferrari has unveiled its one-off livery, paying tribute to Michael Schumacher, for the Formula 1 Italian Grand Prix at Monza
How much will engine upgrade boost Ferrari's chances?
The upgrade will be Ferrari's second on the power unit side this season after they were granted two development opportunities by the FIA.
Formula 1's new 2026 power unit regulations allow engine manufacturers to make upgrades if they are behind on internal combustion engine performance.
After the first Additional Development and Upgrade Opportunities (ADUO) review earlier this year, Ferrari were deemed to be more than four per cent behind benchmark engine manufacturer Red Bull.
Ferrari introduced their first engine upgrade in June's Austrian Grand Prix and will have a second upgrade for their home race at Monza on both cars.
Speaking on The F1 Show podcast, Harry Benjamin believes Lewis Hamilton can take positives away from the Dutch Grand Prix, despite a frustrating result
It means Hamilton and Leclerc will be on their fourth engine of the season, the last before incurring any grid penalties.
"On the performance side, we are introducing an updated power unit as part of the development opportunities available under ADUO," said Ferrari team principal Frederic Vasseur.

"It represents a step in the right direction and as we know this year is very much about marginal gains. Monza is a demanding circuit and the field is extremely close, and our priority will be to execute every aspect of the weekend as well as possible, from Friday onwards.
"We want to draw extra motivation from the passion of our home crowd and give our Tifosi a strong weekend."

detailEn: Qatar GP Qualifying: George Russell bounces back with superb performance to beat Mercedes team-mate Kimi Antonelli to pole position

George Russell beats Kimi Antonelli to pole as Mercedes seal dominant one-two; Lando Norris ahead of Oscar Piastri on second row; Isack Hadjar beats Max Verstappen to fifth; watch the Qatar Grand Prix live on Sky Sports F1 at 4pm on Sunday, with build-up from 2.30pm
George Russell took pole position in Qatar as Kimi Antonelli seemed unhappy with his lap during qualifying
George Russell produced a superb performance in Qatar Grand Prix Qualifying to beat his Mercedes team-mate Kimi Antonelli to pole position.

The reignition of Russell's feud with Max Verstappen at last weekend's Las Vegas Grand Prix had dominated the build-up to the penultimate race of the season, but the Brit produced the perfect response as he topped all three parts of qualifying.

That came as a surprise after Antonelli, who sealed the drivers' title with four rounds to spare, had topped all three practice sessions, but the Italian was unable to match Russell when it mattered most.

Verstappen, who said after winning in Las Vegas last weekend that Russell is "far below" his level, was beaten to fifth by his Red Bull team-mate Isack Hadjar.
Charles Leclerc took seventh but his Ferrari team-mate Lewis Hamilton was beaten to eighth by Racing Bulls' Arvid Lindblad, with the latter's team-mate Liam Lawson completing the top ten.

detailEn: Qatar GP: Kimi Antonelli fastest in final practice from George Russell as Mercedes domination continues ahead of qualifying

Kimi Antonelli led George Russell in another Mercedes one-two in final practice at the Lusail International Circuit; watch Qualifying at 6pm later on Saturday and the Qatar Grand Prix at 4pm on Sunday, live on Sky Sports F1

George Russell says Lewis Hamilton is an equally 'ruthless competitor' to Max Verstappen but that his former team-mate has 'incredible values, grace and dignity'. Watch the full interview during Sky Sports F1's live Qatar GP coverage on Sunday
Kimi Antonelli outpaced Mercedes team-mate George Russell in final practice for the Qatar Grand Prix as the Silver Arrows continued to dominate.

Antonelli, who topped both of Friday's practice sessions, outpaced Russell by 0.249s and it looks highly likely a Mercedes driver will be on pole position after qualifying, which takes place later on Saturday at 6pm (build-up from 5.15pm), live on Sky Sports F1.
Mercedes appear to have a half-second advantage over the rest field as Max Verstappen was 0.510s adrift of Antonelli and the other Red Bull of Isack Hadjar was 0.687s behind.

Mercedes' dominance is a surprise as nearly every race following August's summer break has been very competitive at the front but it seems a combination of the smooth, high-speed track layout and Mercedes finally getting on top of their upgrades from a month ago has given them a significant margin on their rivals.
"Mercedes are almost in a class of their own, so it's worth the rest looking at the gap to Verstappen [in third]," said Sky Sports F1's Bernie Collins.

Ferrari had a difficult Friday after a spin for Charles Leclerc and an engine issue for Lewis Hamilton, but Leclerc fared better in final practice in fifth, ahead of McLaren's Lando Norris and Oscar Piastri.
Hamilton was unhappy throughout the session and stated his "car won't turn" after his final flying lap which put him in ninth, in between Racing Bulls duo Arvid Lindblad and Liam Lawson.
